title: PFGateway TLS Certificate Expiry causing 100% traffic drop
root_cause: The TLS certificate for PFGateway expired without auto-renewal triggering due to a misconfigured Key Vault access policy. The rotation runbook had an outdated service principal reference.
mitigation_steps: Identify the expired certificate CN via: az keyvault certificate show --vault-name <vault> --name <cert-name>
Manually renew the certificate: az keyvault certificate create --vault-name <vault> --name <cert-name> --policy @policy.json
Update the gateway certificate binding: kubectl rollout restart deployment/pf-gateway -n pf-system
Verify TLS handshakes resume: curl -v https://<gateway-endpoint>/health
Update Key Vault access policy to include the correct MSI for auto-rotation
lessons_learned: All certificate rotations must be tested in staging 30 days prior. Auto-renewal alerts should fire at 60, 30, and 7 days before expiry.

title: PFOrchestrator OOM crash loop after memory leak in job processor
root_cause: A recent deployment of PFOrchestrator v2.3.1 introduced a memory leak in the JobProcessor class where event handlers were not deregistered after job completion, leading to unbounded memory growth.
mitigation_steps: Confirm OOM via: kubectl describe pod -l app=pf-orchestrator -n pf-system | grep -A5 OOMKilled
Roll back to previous stable version: kubectl set image deployment/pf-orchestrator orchestrator=pfregistry.azurecr.io/orchestrator:v2.3.0
Monitor memory usage: kubectl top pods -n pf-system --sort-by memory
Drain in-flight jobs before rollback to avoid corruption: kubectl exec -it <pod> -- ./drain-jobs.sh
Verify orchestrator health endpoint returns 200: curl http://pf-orchestrator/health
lessons_learned: Memory profiling gates added to CI/CD pipeline. Load tests now run for 2 hours to detect slow leaks.

title: PFStorageService CosmosDB throttling causing widespread job failures
root_cause: A bulk data migration job ran during peak traffic hours and consumed 95% of provisioned RUs on the shared CosmosDB collection, causing 429 throttling errors for all other PF services.
mitigation_steps: Check CosmosDB metrics for RU consumption: az cosmosdb metrics list --name <account> --resource-group <rg>
Identify the offending partition/query via Azure Portal Metrics Explorer (filter by StatusCode=429)
Pause the migration job: kubectl delete job pf-data-migration -n pf-jobs
Increase RU capacity temporarily: az cosmosdb sql container throughput update --throughput 50000
Restart affected services to clear retry queues: kubectl rollout restart deployment/pf-worker-pool pf-orchestrator -n pf-system
Schedule migration job during off-peak hours with RU limits configured
lessons_learned: Bulk jobs must run in off-peak windows with explicit RU budget limits. Separate CosmosDB collections for batch vs real-time workloads.

title: PFConfigService AppConfiguration refresh loop causing CPU spike
root_cause: A configuration change pushed to Azure App Configuration triggered an infinite refresh loop in PFConfigService due to a missing cache TTL validation. The service consumed 100% CPU and stopped responding to health checks.
mitigation_steps: Check AppConfiguration recent changes: az appconfig revision list --name <config-name> --datetime '2024-09-03T00:00:00Z'
Revert the problematic config change via Azure Portal or CLI
Restart PFConfigService: kubectl rollout restart deployment/pf-config-service -n pf-system
If PFGateway is also impacted, restart it after config service is healthy
Validate config endpoints return correct values: curl http://pf-config-service/config/health
lessons_learned: AppConfiguration changes must be validated in staging first. Config refresh cache TTL minimum enforced at 30 seconds.

title: ServiceBus namespace exhaustion causing PFScheduler job queue backup
root_cause: Azure Service Bus namespace hit the maximum message count limit (80GB) because dead-letter queue messages were never purged. New messages were rejected, causing job scheduling to halt.
mitigation_steps: Check Service Bus namespace usage: az servicebus namespace show --name <ns> --resource-group <rg>
Check dead-letter queue depth: az servicebus queue show --name <queue-name> --namespace-name <ns>
Purge dead-letter queue (use Azure Portal or Service Bus Explorer tool)
Scale up namespace tier if needed: az servicebus namespace update --sku Premium
Restart PFScheduler: kubectl rollout restart deployment/pf-scheduler -n pf-system
Verify job queue is draining: watch -n5 'az servicebus queue show --name pf-jobs --namespace-name <ns> | jq .messageCount'
lessons_learned: Dead-letter queue purge automation added. Namespace capacity alerts added at 70% and 85% thresholds.

title: AAD token acquisition failures causing PFGateway authentication outage
root_cause: Azure Active Directory experienced a regional outage in East US, causing PFGateway to fail all authentication requests. The gateway did not have an AAD token cache with sufficient TTL to survive the outage window.
mitigation_steps: Confirm AAD status on Azure Status Page: https://status.azure.com
Check AAD token cache hit rate in Application Insights: requests | where name contains 'token'
If AAD is the root cause, failover traffic to West US cluster: az traffic-manager endpoint update --status Enabled --name westus-endpoint
Enable emergency bypass mode if configured: kubectl set env deployment/pf-gateway AAD_BYPASS_MODE=emergency
Notify customers via status page and internal channels
lessons_learned: AAD token cache TTL extended to 1 hour. Cross-region failover runbook now automated with Traffic Manager health probes.
